rules: A pattern is a method. It may suggest a structure; it never states a fact about an organisation.
Every element a pattern suggests still needs the organisation's own evidence. Without it, the element is an assumption, with what breaks if it is false.
A pattern never raises the label of a statement, never closes an unknown and never settles a contradiction.
A pattern names role-types, never persons, holders or numbers of people.
This catalogue holds no organisation's data and no copied text. Each pattern is a plain description of a widely known way to organise.

patterns.name: Functional organisation
patterns.summary: Work is grouped by kind of expertise, such as sales, operations, finance and people. Each function has one accountable lead, and the top role joins the functions together.
typical_capabilities: Support services, such as legal, premises and information

decision_rights.role_type: the top role, advised by the finance lead

decision_rights.decision: Methods and standards inside a function

typical_hand_offs.what_crosses: a confirmed order or commitment to deliver

fits_when: There is one main line of products or services.
The organisation serves one market or a few similar ones.
Depth of expertise matters more than speed across functions.
does_not_fit_when: There are several distinct product lines or markets that need their own priorities.
Most work needs fast coordination across many functions every day.
known_risks: Each function serves its own goals before the whole.
Decisions that cross functions are slow and pile up at the top role.
No one owns a customer's whole experience.
